Read an isobaric (TMT, TMTpro, iTRAQ, DiLeu) design out of an SDRF, or every reason it cannot be read

sdrf_isobaric_design.Rd

Read an isobaric (TMT, TMTpro, iTRAQ, DiLeu) experimental design out of an SDRF, one row per file and annotated channel, in MetaMorpheus's terms, or every reason it was refused.

Answers can this SDRF drive an isobaric quantification, and which sample is in which channel of which file? Calls mzLib's SdrfIsobaricDesign.Read. It runs MetaMorpheus's own checks on a TMT design - one plex, fraction and technical replicate per file; a channel described once per plex; no sample twice at one fraction in a plex - and refuses rather than repairs, reporting every failure at once.

Usage

sdrf_isobaric_design(path, kit = NULL, plex_column = NULL,
  plex_file_name_pattern = NULL, single_plex = NULL, condition_columns = NULL,
  searched_files = NULL, out = NULL, timeout = 60)

Arguments

path

Path to a .sdrf.tsv file.

kit

The kit the search used, named as isobaric_kits takes it ("TMT10", "tmt18", "TMT6-plex", "TMT11 on K"). NULL sends none, and mzLib then refuses: the kit is never guessed from the labels.

plex_column

The column each row's plex is read from, by its exact name.

plex_file_name_pattern

A .NET regular expression matched, ignoring case, against each row's file name; the plex is its group named plex, else its first group, e.g. "TMT_?pool(?<plex>\\d+)" (one backslash in the pattern, two in R source).

single_plex

The name of the one plex every file belongs to.

condition_columns

The factor value[...] columns that make up the condition, exactly as for sdrf_design. NULL uses the document's only factor column.

searched_files

The files the search will read, exactly as for sdrf_design: each must be named exactly by some row. A search that read X-calib.mzML for an SDRF naming X.raw matches nothing; sdrf_restrict the SDRF first.

out

A folder, created when missing. mzLib writes MetaMorpheus's TmtDesign.txt (1-based) inside it, replacing one already there, but only when the design is valid. MetaMorpheus reads it only from the folder of the first spectra file.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

It guesses nothing: not the kit, because one kit's labels can be a subset of another's, and not the plex, which you declare with exactly one of plex_column, plex_file_name_pattern and single_plex. Giving none, or several, is mzLib's refusal.

Channel labels are read by mzLib's SdrfIsobaricLabels, the rule isobaric_kits's sdrf_label writes: for TMT10, TMT131 (PRIDE's spelling of the last channel) names 131N (mzLib #1467); for TMT11, where 131N and 131C are both channels, it is still refused.

The numbers are 1-based, as the SDRF writes them. sdrf_design's are 0-based. That split is mzLib's, and mzLibR converts neither.

Value

An mzlibr_sdrf_isobaric_design. is_valid is TRUE when there are no refusals. A refusal is an answer, not an error: refusals then lists every reason at once, in mzLib's words, and records has no rows.

kit is the kit name exactly as you gave it, and kit_type mzLib's name for the kit it resolved to ("TMT10", "TMT18", "iTRAQ4", ...), as isobaric_kits names it; both NA when no kit was given. kit_channels lists every channel of the kit in reporter m/z order (a channel here and absent from records is one the SDRF does not annotate), NULL without a kit. plex_column, plex_file_name_pattern and single_plex echo the plex source you gave, NA for the others; plex_source is where mzLib read the plex from, as its report prints it, "(not declared)" when no single source could be used. plex_ids is a named vector, plex name to its number, 1 to N in case-insensitive name order (the order MetaMorpheus numbers plexes in), empty when refused; plex_count counts the plexes, 0 when refused. file_key_column is the column files were keyed on - comment[searched data file] when the SDRF has it, else comment[data file] - or NA when it has neither. condition_columns lists the columns the condition was built from; condition_columns_declared and searched_files_given say whether you passed them. file_count counts the files in the design and record_count the rows of records, one per file and annotated channel; both 0 when refused. notes says what was dropped or filled on the way; report is mzLib's account of all of it, to print. written is a list (path of the TmtDesign.txt, file_count, record_count), or NULL when out was not given or the design was refused. caveats says what the design does and does not cover.

records is a data.frame, files in SDRF row order, then each file's channels in reporter m/z order: full_path (the searched path you passed for the file, else the file name the SDRF gives); plex, as the declared source gives it; plex_id, the plex's number in plex_ids; sample_name, the SDRF source name of the sample in the channel; channel, as the kit spells it ("127N"); condition, the condition columns' values joined with _; and biological_replicate (as written, never ranked), fraction (1 when the SDRF has no fraction column) and technical_replicate (1 when it has no technical-replicate column), all 1-based.

Restrict first, then read the design

A search reads X-calib.mzML where the SDRF names the acquired X.raw, so searched_files of the search's own names match nothing. sdrf_restrict joins the two and writes the searched name into comment[searched data file], and this function keys on that column when a document has it.

Wraps

Wire verb sdrf isobaric-design. Generated from the bridge's verb spec sdrf.isobaric-design.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • SdrfIsobaricDesign.WriteTmtDesign in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfIsobaricDesign.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfIsobaricDesign.PlexIds in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfIsobaricDesign.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfIsobaricDesign.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfIsobaricFile in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfIsobaricDesign.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfIsobaricChannel in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfIsobaricDesign.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • IsobaricMassTag.TryGetTagType in mzLib/Omics/Modifications/IsobaricMassTag.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • IsobaricMassTag.TryGetIsobaricMassTag in mzLib/Omics/Modifications/IsobaricMassTag.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

path

path; required. One .sdrf.tsv file. A file that does not exist is a usage error.

kit

string; default absent. The kit the search used, resolved exactly as isobaric kits --kit resolves it: mzLib's IsobaricMassTag.TryGetTagType, whole name, case-insensitive, optionally followed by " on <motif>" (TMT10, tmt10, TMT6-plex, TMT11 on K), never a substring. It is SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.Tag, which supplies the channel list and their reporter m/z order. A blank or unknown name is a usage error naming the known kits. Absent: mzLib is given no tag and refuses ("No isobaric tag was given"), because the kit is never guessed from the labels.

plex_column (wire --plex-column)

string; default absent. SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.PlexColumn: the column each row's plex is read from, by its exact name. A column not in the SDRF, or a cell that is empty or not available, is mzLib's refusal. Given with no value is a usage error. mzLib needs exactly one of plex-column, plex-file-name-pattern and single-plex; none, or several, is mzLib's refusal, not a usage error.

plex_file_name_pattern (wire --plex-file-name-pattern)

string; default absent. SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.PlexFileNamePattern: a .NET regular expression matched, ignoring case, against each row's file name (the key column's, comment[searched data file] else comment[data file]). The plex is its group named plex, else its first group. A pattern that does not parse, has no group, or does not match a file name is mzLib's refusal. Given with no value is a usage error.

single_plex (wire --single-plex)

string; default absent. SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.SinglePlex: the name of the one plex every file belongs to. Given with no value is a usage error.

condition_columns (wire --condition-columns)

string; default absent. SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.ConditionColumns, exactly as sdrf design takes it: the factor value[...] columns the condition is built from, by exact name, separated by TAB characters, in join order; the condition is their values joined with "_". Absent: mzLib uses the document's only factor column, and refuses a document with several. Given but blank, or with a blank name, is a usage error.

searched_files (wire --searched-files-stdin)

flag; default absent. SdrfIsobaricDesignOptions.SearchedFiles, exactly as sdrf design takes it: stdin holds the files the search will read, one per line, as paths or bare names. Each must be named EXACTLY (case and extension) by some row; rows for other files are dropped and reported in notes; the searched paths become full_path. A search that read X-calib.mzML for an SDRF naming X.raw matches no row: run sdrf restrict first, which writes the searched name into comment[searched data file], the column this reader keys on first.

out

path; default absent; range a folder; an existing file is refused. A FOLDER, created when missing (bridge thread 010, PYB-5). mzLib's SdrfIsobaricDesign.WriteTmtDesign writes MetaMorpheus's TmtDesign.txt inside it, replacing one already there: 1-based, one row per file and annotated channel, header SdrfIsobaricDesign.TmtDesignHeader. The file name is MetaMorpheus's (GlobalVariables.TmtExperimentalDesignFileName); mzLib has no constant for it at the pin, so the bridge holds the one copy. Written only when is_valid; a refused design writes nothing and creates no folder, and written is null. A path that is an existing file, or no value, is a usage error, checked before the SDRF is read.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

path

string; never NA. The SDRF path as given.

is_valid

bool; never NA. No refusals. False is an answer, not an error: the table is then empty.

kit

string; NA when --kit was not given (mzLib then refuses). The --kit name exactly as given.

kit_type

string; NA when --kit was not given. The IsobaricMassTagType member the kit resolved to (TMT6, TMT10, TMT11, TMT16, TMT18, iTRAQ4, iTRAQ8, diLeu4, diLeu12 at d10017ce), as isobaric kits names it.

kit_channels

string[]; NA when --kit was not given. Every channel label of the kit, in reporter m/z order (IsobaricMassTag.ChannelLabels). A channel here and absent from the table is one the SDRF does not annotate.

plex_column

string; NA when --plex-column was not given. The plex column as given.

plex_file_name_pattern

string; NA when --plex-file-name-pattern was not given. The pattern as given.

single_plex

string; NA when --single-plex was not given. The single plex as given.

plex_source

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricDesign.PlexSource: where the plex was read from, as mzLib's report prints it; (not declared) when no single source could be used.

plex_ids

object; never NA. SdrfIsobaricDesign.PlexIds: plex name to its IsobaricQuantSampleInfo.PlexId, 1..N in case-insensitive name order (MetaMorpheus's ToMzLibDesign rule), listed in id order. Empty when refused.

plex_count

int; in plexes; never NA. Entries in plex_ids; 0 when refused.

file_key_column

string; NA when the SDRF has neither comment[searched data file] nor comment[data file], so no row names a file (also a refusal). The column files were keyed on: comment[searched data file] when present, else comment[data file] (MAP-12).

condition_columns

string[]; never NA. The factor columns the condition was built from, in join order; empty when none could be chosen.

condition_columns_declared

bool; never NA. Whether --condition-columns was given.

searched_files_given

bool; never NA. Whether --searched-files-stdin was given.

file_count

int; in files; never NA. Files in the design (SdrfIsobaricDesign.Files); 0 when refused.

record_count

int; in rows; never NA. Rows in the table: one per file and annotated channel; 0 when refused.

refusals

string[]; never NA. Every reason the design was refused, all at once, in mzLib's words. Empty when valid.

notes

string[]; never NA. What was dropped or filled on the way to a valid design: rows dropped because the search does not read their file, and a file with no row of its own for one of its plex's channels.

report

string; never NA. mzLib's human-readable account (SdrfIsobaricDesign.Report): counts and kit, key column, plex source, condition columns, sample type, notes, refusals.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. Column name to one value per file and annotated channel: files in SDRF row order, then each file's channels in reporter m/z order.

written

object; NA when --out was not given, or the design was refused and nothing was written. {path, file_count, record_count} of the TmtDesign.txt written; path is the --out folder joined with TmtDesign.txt.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Eight static caveats.

Columns of records

full_path

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricFile.FilePath: the matching searched path when --searched-files-stdin was given, else the file name the key column gives.

plex

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricFile.Plex: the plex as the declared source gives it (a column cell, a pattern's group, or the single plex).

plex_id

int; never NA. The plex's entry in plex_ids, 1-based: the PlexId mzLib's quantification design gives it.

sample_name

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricChannel.SampleName: the SDRF source name.

channel

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricChannel.Label: the channel as the kit spells it (127N), whatever form the SDRF's comment[label] used (TMT127N, NT=TMT127N;AC=...).

condition

string; never NA. SdrfIsobaricChannel.Condition: the condition columns' values joined with _.

biological_replicate

int; never NA. SdrfIsobaricChannel.BiologicalReplicate: 1-based, as the SDRF writes it, never ranked or shifted.

fraction

int; never NA. SdrfIsobaricFile.Fraction: 1-based, as written; 1 when the SDRF has no comment[fraction identifier] column (mzLib's SdrfDesignRules).

technical_replicate

int; never NA. SdrfIsobaricFile.TechnicalReplicate: 1-based, as written; 1 when the SDRF has no comment[technical replicate] column.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

path missing or the file does not exist

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--kit without a value, or a name mzLib cannot resolve (the same message isobaric kits --kit gives)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--plex-column, --plex-file-name-pattern or --single-plex without a value; --condition-columns without a value or with a blank name

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--out without a value, or naming an existing file (checked before the SDRF is read)

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

mzLib cannot parse the SDRF at all, or the --out folder cannot be created or written

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • 1-BASED, as written. fraction, technical_replicate and biological_replicate are the SDRF's own numbers, as mzLib's SdrfIsobaricDesign keeps them and TmtDesign.txt holds them. sdrf design is 0-based (mzLib's SpectraFileInfo). The split is mzLib's, and the bridge converts neither table: never mix the two without adding or removing 1.

  • is_valid = false is an answer: refusals lists every reason at once and the table is empty. A missing kit, no plex source, two plex sources and a bad pattern are refusals, not errors.

  • Nothing is guessed. The kit is only the one named, because one kit's labels can be a subset of another's (TMT11 with 131C unannotated reads exactly like TMT10). The plex is only the source declared; comment[sample preparation batch] is often not a plex (in PXD061609 it holds three fractionation arms of one plex).

  • Rows are the annotated channels only. mzLib's quantification design (ToExperimentalDesign) carries every kit channel, an unannotated one with biological replicate 0 and no sample; that design is not on the wire.

  • A plex is one channel-to-sample map: every file of a plex carries all of its channels, so fractions share their samples.

  • Channel labels are read through mzLib's SdrfIsobaricLabels, one rule for readers and writers. For TMT10, TMT131 (PRIDE's spelling of the last channel) names 131N (since mzLib #1467); TMT131 is still refused for TMT11, where 131N and 131C are both channels.

  • Sample type is not read (mzLib MAP-08): every annotated channel is a study sample, a reference or pool channel included.

  • --out names a folder. MetaMorpheus reads TmtDesign.txt only from the folder of the first spectra file, and refuses a folder that also holds ExperimentalDesign.tsv. mzLib's writer replaces an existing TmtDesign.txt; MetaMorpheus's own --sdrfDesign never does.

  • TMT16 is mzLib's TMTpro 16-plex. MetaMorpheus searches it with its TMT18 label; a TMT16 design is read as is by such a run, with 134C and 135N empty.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.sdrf.isobaric_design

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::sdrf::isobaric_design_with with IsobaricDesignOptions

  • R (mzLibR): sdrf_isobaric_design

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: TmtDesign.txt is MetaMorpheus's name (GlobalVariables.TmtExperimentalDesignFileName), and mzLib publishes no constant for it at d10017ce, so the bridge holds the one copy (Sdrf.TmtDesignFileName). Ask mzLib for SdrfIsobaricDesign.TmtDesignFileName, or a WriteTmtDesign overload that takes the folder, and read the name from there.

  • No --paths-stdin form, for the reason sdrf design gives: the kit, the plex source, the condition columns and the searched files are per-deposit facts.

  • mzLib's quantification design (ToExperimentalDesign: every kit channel with its reporter m/z, an unannotated one with biological replicate 0) is not projected. Add it when a bridge verb quantifies reporter ions from it.

References

  • doi:10.1038/s41467-021-26111-3: SDRF-Proteomics, the format read (Dai et al., Nat Commun 12, 5854, 2021)

Examples


# PXD008841 writes no plex column; the plex survives only in the file names, spelled two ways
# (TMTpool1, TMT_pool5), so one pattern reads both:
d <- sdrf_isobaric_design("PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv", kit = "TMT10",
  plex_file_name_pattern = "TMT_?pool(?<plex>\\d+)")
d
#> <mzlibr_sdrf_isobaric_design> PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv: 4 files, 2 plex(es), kit TMT10, 40 channel rows (1-based numbers)
#>   plex from: file-name pattern 'TMT_?pool(?<plex>\d+)' (declared)
#>   files keyed on: comment[data file]
d$plex_ids
#> 1 5 
#> 1 2 
d$records[10, c("channel", "sample_name", "plex_id", "fraction", "biological_replicate")]
#>    channel sample_name plex_id fraction biological_replicate
#> 10    131N        pool       1        1                    1

# Declare no plex source and mzLib refuses rather than guess one:
refused <- sdrf_isobaric_design("PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv", kit = "TMT10")
refused$is_valid
#> [1] FALSE
writeLines(strwrap(refused$refusals[[1]], 90))
#> No plex source was declared. Name the column that holds the plex, give a file-name
#> pattern whose group captures it, or name the single plex. The plex is never inferred
#> (MAP-09): 'comment[sample preparation batch]' is often not a plex.
